title: Amazon broadcast details: Prime Vision, Rapid Recap, more features on platform's first NBA playoffs coverage
article_content:
Amazon Prime Video has launched its first-ever NBA playoff coverage (beginning April 18, 2026) following a landmark media rights deal. Central to the broadcast is "Prime Vision," an AI-enhanced viewing mode that provides real-time tactical overlays. The AI model analyzes player positioning to identify mismatches—such as a size advantage or a defensive lapse—and highlights them for viewers using on-screen graphic circles.

In addition to live tactical analysis, the platform utilizes AWS-powered advanced statistics to provide "Rapid Recap" and "Key Moments" features. These tools use machine learning to automatically curate highlight reels, bringing late-arriving fans up to speed by identifying the most significant plays based on momentum shifts and scoring impact. The broadcast also integrates personalized bet tracking via FanDuel, further demonstrating how AI is being used to create a more interactive and data-rich "second-screen" experience for sports fans.

additional_sources.title: Prime Video Exclusively Presents the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament Plus First-and Second-Round Playoff Games
additional_sources.article_content:
Amazon announced its exclusive Prime Video presentation of the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament and first- and second-round playoff games, positioning the launch as a major milestone in its NBA rights rollout. The release adds complementary detail on the broader production package around the AI features, including scheduling, studio programming, and the structure of NBA on Prime broadcasts. It confirms that Prime Vision is part of a wider viewer-experience stack rather than a standalone overlay, and it frames the launch as an official platform initiative tied to Amazon’s long-term sports media strategy.

The added source is useful because it supplies the official announcement angle: it situates Prime Vision, Rapid Recap, and AI-generated viewing enhancements within Amazon’s overall programming plan, helping a writer distinguish between editorial coverage of the features and Amazon’s own positioning of them as product differentiators for live sports streaming.
